Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council wished Councilmember Ramirez a Happy Birthday. Councilmember
Ramirez reported on his attendance at the Los Angeles Sanitation District Meeting, City
employee Maria Corona’s retirement party, Teen Alliance Program (TAP) Anniversary
Scholarship and Recognition Dinner and thanked Parks and Recreation staff for a
successful event. Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at the Mayor’s
Prayer Breakfast, and the Egg-Stravagant Egg Hunt; shared she met with the Maverick
Group and toured Home2 Suite hotel; met with a representative from Southeast Water
Coalition along with Glen Kau, Director of Public Services/City Engineer, and Jaqueline
Koontz, Public Services Senior Civil Engineer, to discuss various topics about water and
she will have a representative present at the upcoming commissioners meeting on
May 29; acknowledged TAP’s 20 years of success and thanked Rosie Lozoya,
Recreation and Park Services Supervisor, for being an integral part of that program. Vice
Mayor Perez shared that City newsletters were distributed; reported on her attendance at
the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast, the Egg-Stravagant Egg Hunt, League of California Cities
City Leaders Summit where she advocated for Proposition 36, homelessness initiatives,
and Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl substance concerns; the California Joint Powers
Insurance Authority Risk Management Conference; and wished all a Happy Mother’s Day.
Mayor Ayala reported on his attendance at the Arbor Day event and thanked all staff
involved that made it educational and a success; thanked the Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs
Soroptimist organization that continually host exceptional events that contribute to the
community.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council proclaimed May as Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month and
presented a proclamation to Madeline Arenas, a featured artist at the Mary Paxon Gallery,
and Loida Moreno, President of the International Club.

SUBJECT: AGREEMENT FOR PEST CONTROL SERVICES FOR CITY FACILITIES

Background:

The City addresses pest control services at individual facilities on an as-needed basis, and a
few select facilities have ongoing service agreements. While this approach has addressed
immediate concerns, it has resulted in various service levels across facilities.

To promote consistency, improve preventive maintenance, and better manage potential pest-
related issues proactively, staff evaluated the need for a citywide pest control service and
determined it would be in the best interest of the City to go out to bid for all facilities.

On September 23, 2024 staff issued a request for quotes (RFQ #25-3101-002) and reviewed
bids from multiple vendors. On October 4, 2024 four bids were received with the following results:

Background:

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) is currently transitioning its radio system
to the Los Angeles Regional Interoperable Communications System (LA-RICS). To maintain
access to LASD communications networks, the City must also update its own radio system to
meet LA-RICS requirements.

LA-RICS is designed to significantly improve both radio and broadband communication
capabilities for police, fire, paramedics, and other emergency responders across Los Angeles
County. This system creates a unified communications network, removes barriers to multi-
jurisdictional response efforts, and enables direct communication between personnel from
different agencies. As part of this modernization, LA-RICS mandates that each radio be assigned
to a single officer to ensure system security and accountability.

Historically, Norwalk’s Public Safety Officers have shared radios between shifts. However, to
comply with LA-RICS requirements, the City will need to purchase 25 additional radios so that
each officer can be issued their own. Several of the City’s current radios can be updated to meet
LA-RICS standards, while those that cannot will be repurposed for general operations within
other City departments.

SUBJECT: CITYWIDE CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION STUDY

Background:

At the direction of City Council, the City initiated a comprehensive classification and
compensation study in partnership with TrueComp and CPS HR Consulting. This marks the first
formal review of the City's classification and compensation study.

The study evaluated job families, career fields, and classification titles to assess market
competitiveness, internal equity, and structural alignment.

Over the past nine months, the consultants have thoroughly studied compensation models
across comparable cities, including Carson, Downey, Gardena, Pico Rivera, Torrance and
Whittier. This benchmark aligned Norwalk’s compensation practices with the broader public
sector market.

During the study, key issues were identified, including internal equity discrepancies among
positions, market competitiveness of salaries, pay compaction within job classifications,
stagnation for employees at the top of the pay scale, and challenges in employee retention and
talent attraction.

CPS HR representatives will present their methodology and findings, providing data-driven
recommendations to support equitable, competitive, and sustainable compensation practices.

the annual budget.
